Walmart earlier officially announced it will finally begin rolling out Apple Pay after delaying it for more than a decade.

When will your nearby Walmart store start accepting Apple Pay? I have obtained the full rollout plan; here's everything...

Walmart Apple Pay rollout timeline

Walmart said in today's announcement that Apple Pay and broader contactless payment support will begin rolling out starting next week, with full availability across all U.S. stores by the end of this year.

According to an internal memo Walmart sent to store management today, obtained by 9to5Mac, the retailer provided more detailed phased rollout specifics. The company currently plans to roll out state by state. These dates may shift if any issues arise during the rollout. Here's the current roadmap:

States Tap to Pay Launch Arkansas Aug. 24–31 California, Washington, Oregon, Nevada, Idaho, Alaska, Hawaii Sept. 10 Kansas, Louisiana, Nebraska, Oklahoma Sept. 14 Texas Sept. 17 Arizona, Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, South Dakota, Montana, North Dakota, Wyoming Sept. 21 Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa Sept. 24 Tennessee, Indiana, Michigan, Kentucky Sept. 28 Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi Oct. 1 Florida Oct. 5 North Carolina, Virginia, South Carolina, West Virginia, Puerto Rico Oct. 8 Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, Maryland, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Maine, Delaware, Rhode Island, Vermont, District of Columbia Oct. 12

It appears Missouri is currently absent from Walmart's timeline for reasons unknown.

In the memo, Walmart also listed all the contactless payment methods it will support:

  • Contactless-enabled credit and debit cards
  • Digital wallets, including Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay
  • Payment-capable smartwatches and wearables
  • Supported contactless EBT cards

Walmart's adoption of Apple Pay is long overdue. Does this change where you choose to shop? Let us know in the comments.
